tldr: WaltzRL is a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains a conversation agent and a feedback agent in a collaborative positive-sum game, using a Dynamic Improvement Reward to reduce both unsafe responses and overrefusals in LLMs.
contributions: Proposed WaltzRL, a multi-agent RL framework that jointly optimizes a conversation agent and a feedback agent for safety alignment
Introduced a novel Dynamic Improvement Reward (DIR) formulation that incentivizes the feedback agent to produce suggestions that genuinely improve the conversation agent's responses
Demonstrated that WaltzRL enhances LLM safety without degrading general capabilities, lifting the Pareto front between helpfulness and harmlessness
methods: WaltzRL formulates safety alignment as a collaborative multi-agent reinforcement learning game between a conversation agent and a feedback agent. The feedback agent labels responses for unsafe content and overrefusal, provides textual feedback, and adaptively decides when to stop giving feedback. A Dynamic Improvement Reward (DIR) is computed as the difference in the conversation agent's reward before and after incorporating feedback, encouraging useful suggestions. Training uses a two-stage pipeline: first freezing the conversation agent to train the feedback agent, then collaborative training with both agents. The system is initialized with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and trained on adversarial prompts from WildJailbreak and borderline overrefusal prompts from OR-Bench-80K.
results: On WildJailbreak, unsafe responses decreased from 39.0% to 4.6%. On OR-Bench, overrefusals decreased from 45.3% to 9.9%, evaluated across five diverse datasets. The framework was shown to preserve general capability even without including helpfulness data during RL training. An oracle baseline using template feedback from ground-truth labels underperformed WaltzRL, demonstrating the importance of detailed feedback.
limitations: Training was conducted without helpfulness data, relying solely on adversarial and borderline prompts
Only one feedback round (T_max=1) was used, though the framework theoretically supports multiple rounds
At inference, both agents must be deployed jointly, which may increase system complexity compared to single-model approaches
